title: Productivity and firm exit during the COVID-19 crisis: cross-country evidence
study_data: WBES survey+follow-up across 34 countries; 2019/2020 baseline, up to three follow-up rounds
outcome_stock_flow: Binary confirmed/assumed firm exit; baseline fixed-asset purchase indicator used as covariate
statistical_model: Logit with controls, fixed effects, marginal effects, cluster-robust errors
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: Confirmed versus assumed closure and covariate adjustments
transfer_to_fer: Closest WBES methodological comparator; missing survey interview does NOT prove firm exit

title: Short-term financial constraints and SMEs’ investment decision
study_data: France credit-access survey + FIBEN 2012–16; 92,488 survey-quarter observations, 7,778 independent firms; 5,652 firms in investment panel
outcome_stock_flow: Investment flow / lagged total asset stock; binary indicators of credit constraints
statistical_model: Heckman selection probit and dynamic system GMM; matching, quantile regressions
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: J-test, AR2 serial correlation, alternative instrumental variables, matching
transfer_to_fer: Strong formal model/diagnostics comparator; NOT appropriate to copy system GMM with two WBES waves

title: ECB unconventional monetary policy and SME access to finance
study_data: ECB/EC SAFE, 11,319 SME survey observations, 2014–19, stressed euro-area countries
outcome_stock_flow: Binary credit constraint outcome, not fixed asset purchasing
statistical_model: Probit with sample-selection adjustment; leverage/risk interaction, lagged monetary-policy exposure and controls
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: Alternative constraints and monetary proxies, age/size subgroups and countries
transfer_to_fer: Model to results to scoped policy discussion; NO direct monetary shock inference for Hungary

title: Tightening monetary policy and investment dynamics in the European Monetary Union
study_data: Amadeus non-listed-firm panel 2011–21, 130,313 firms across 19 euro-area economies
outcome_stock_flow: Capital accumulation/investment response to monetary surprises
statistical_model: Dynamic local projections; firm FE, sector-year FE, leverage × shocks and country factors
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: Heterogeneity by leverage, debt maturity and credit environment; macro-period robustness
transfer_to_fer: Best policy-identification contrast: not reproducible with 2019/2023 binary WBES alone

title: Dynamic Olley-Pakes productivity decomposition with entry and exit
study_data: Slovenian manufacturing 1995–2000: 3,867 firms in 1995, 4,580 in 2000, 2,677 surviving firms
outcome_stock_flow: Aggregate productivity, weighted market shares; real firm entry/exit
statistical_model: Algebraic additive decomposition: survivors, true entrants and exiters; compare conventions
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: Alternative productivity and weights, appendix formulas
transfer_to_fer: Borrow clarity of identities and limitations; sample leavers in Hungary are NOT economic exits

title: Accounting for Nonignorable Unit Nonresponse and Attrition in Panel Studies with Refreshment Samples
journal: Journal of Survey Statistics and Methodology
access_status: Full author manuscript text (journal version not compared)
study_data: Simulation + AP/Yahoo 2007–08 election panel with refreshment interviews
outcome_stock_flow: Nonresponse and attrition probabilities; no corporate-investment dependent variable
statistical_model: Bayesian additive-nonignorable selection and joint-data model; sensitivity analysis
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: Assumptions on baseline and refreshment unit nonresponse
transfer_to_fer: Demonstrates selection models need assumptions; IPW alone cannot remove MNAR selection

title: Do loan subsidies boost the real activity of small firms?
access_status: Publisher introduction, abstracts and section previews only
study_data: Hungarian MNB subsidy programme (2013), linked bank-credit registry and corporate financial records
outcome_stock_flow: Real investment, employment and firm efficiency—not binary WBES purchase participation
statistical_model: Propensity-score matching, counterfactual programme evaluation and simulation-based robustness (as described in publisher preview)
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: Programme access heterogeneity and alternative simulation assessment
transfer_to_fer: Best local economic-policy comparison; its treatment effect is not transferable to our dataset

title: As the market churns: productivity and firm exit in developing countries
access_status: Published abstract only; World Bank precursor available
study_data: World Bank Enterprise Surveys panel in 47 economies
outcome_stock_flow: Firm market exit vs unresolved operating status
statistical_model: Firm-exit predictors and uncertainty corrections (from abstract); exact published regression not yet extracted
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: Alternative classification of firms with uncertain operating status
transfer_to_fer: Cite conservative true-closure definition; do not claim non-interviews are firm deaths

title: Nonignorable Attrition in Multi-Period Panels With Refreshment Samples
access_status: Published abstract only; older working paper available
study_data: Longitudinal survey selection with refreshment sample, multiple periods
diagnostics_or_sensitivity: Sensitivity of identification to additional model assumptions
transfer_to_fer: Methodological foundation; refreshment does not nonparametrically solve all missingness

title: Financial constraints on investment: Effects of firm size and the financial crisis
journal: Research in International Business and Finance
access_status: Published abstract plus indexed article excerpts only
study_data: United Kingdom manufacturing survey around financial crisis
outcome_stock_flow: Fixed-investment intentions, NOT realised asset purchases
statistical_model: Size-heterogeneous regressions; indexed excerpt discusses Hausman endogeneity test
transfer_to_fer: Strong outcome-type caution: planned vs actual vs binary purchase measures differ

title: Using Administrative Data to Evaluate Sampling Bias in a Business Panel Survey
study_data: Bank of Italy Invind panel ~4,000 firms per year 2002–13 matched to financial statements
outcome_stock_flow: Firm performance indicators and sample entry/attrition
statistical_model: Administrative benchmarking of survey estimates and weight-vintage sensitivity
transfer_to_fer: BEST direct survey-composition comparator; journal Q2 in SCImago 2025, never call it Q1
